### Observed differences

- In the earlier window the sequence A21 → A22 → A23 ran in every trace: A22 appeared in all 200 traces, always directly after A21, and A23 followed two positions after A21. In the later window A22 appears in only about 46 in 100 traces, and A21's outgoing transitions are redistributed: about 46 in 100 still go to A22, about 33 in 100 go to A28 and about 21 in 100 go to A27. [OCC003, DIR001, REL001, LAG001]

- A27 and A28, which did not occur at all in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces), each appear in about 55 in 100 later-window traces (109 of 200). They always appear together and never alongside A22: A22 co-occurs with neither of them, while A27 and A28 co-occur in every trace containing either one. [OCC004, OCC005, REL005, REL006, REL009]

- In the later window the new pair sits between A21 and A23: A21 precedes A27 and A28 in all of their joint appearances with A21, A27 and A28 each precede A23 in about 55 in 100 traces, and the distance from A21 to A23 grows from two positions (always, earlier) to three positions in about 55 in 100 later traces. The internal order of the pair is mixed — A28 before A27 in about 6 of 10 joint appearances, A27 before A28 in about 4 of 10 — and both orders end in A23. [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL007, REL008, REL009, LAG001, DIR002, DIR003]

- Away from this segment, A18 participation fell from about 59 in 100 traces to about 41 in 100, while A19 rose from about 42 in 100 to about 60 in 100. [OCC001, OCC002]

- A21's relative position shifted slightly earlier (mean about 0.46 to about 0.44 of the trace), and A27 and A28 sit at about 0.48 of the trace, just after A21's position — consistent with one extra step being added after A21. [POS001, POS002, POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, roughly 55 in 100 traces replace the previously mandatory A22 step between A21 and A23 with the pair A27 and A28, while the remaining roughly 45 in 100 traces keep the original A21 → A22 → A23 sequence. A22 and the pair A27/A28 behave as mutually exclusive alternatives, and A27 and A28 always run together with a mixed internal order. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR001, REL001, REL005, REL006, REL009, LAG001]

The support is direct and consistent: 19 evidence items were flagged where fewer than 1 would be expected by chance in an unchanged process; routing out of A21, the relations of A22 and of A27/A28 with A21 and A23, and the A21–A23 distance all show the same structure, and each difference is larger than in virtually all random re-splits of the pooled data. Note that many of these items describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. [DIR001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL007, REL008, LAG001, POS001]

Limitations: the evidence cannot show what determines the choice between the two routes — in particular, it cannot distinguish a per-case branch from a shift in the mix of case types between the windows — and it cannot establish whether the A22 route persists beyond this sample. [DIR001, REL005, REL009]

Other differences: A18 participation decreased (about 59 in 100 traces to about 41 in 100) and A19 increased (about 42 in 100 to about 60 in 100); the evidence contains no relational or routing data on these two activities, so their connection to the main change remains unknown. [OCC001, OCC002]
